name: Auction Bridge
description: Auction Bridge is the historic bridge variant that bridged the gap between Bridge Whist and modern Contract Bridge. Unlike modern Bridge, in Auction Bridge, all tricks won above six count toward the game score if the contract is fulfilled, making the bidding process less about strict precision and more about competition for the trump suit.

overview.description: Auction Bridge is the historic bridge variant that bridged the gap between Bridge Whist and modern Contract Bridge. Unlike modern Bridge, in Auction Bridge, all tricks won above six count toward the game score if the contract is fulfilled, making the bidding process less about strict precision and more about competition for the trump suit.

history.origins: Developed in the late 19th century as an improvement over Bridge Whist, where the dealer chose trumps. Auction introduced competitive bidding. It was reportedly formalized by members of the Bath Club in London and popularized in India.
timeline: 1904: First formal rules of Auction Bridge published.
1910s: Becomes the most popular social card game in English-speaking countries.
1925: Gradually superseded by Contract Bridge, which rewarded precise bidding more heavily.
Present: Occasionally played by bridge historians and in traditional social circles.
history.cultural: A staple of the Edwardian era, Auction Bridge was the definitive 'Game of the Elite' before the Great Depression.
history.evolution: The most significant evolution was moving the scoring of overtricks 'below the line', a rule changed in Contract Bridge to penalize under-bidding.

setup.deck: Standard 52-card deck. Ranks A(high)-2(low). Suit priorities: No Trumps, Spades, Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs.
setup.dealing: The entire deck is dealt out, 13 cards per player.
setup.equipment: Standard pack, score sheet with a line drawn horizontally in the middle.

rules.objective: Score 'Below the Line' points by winning tricks to reach 30 points for a 'Game'. Win two games to win the 'Rubber'.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Lead**: Player to declarer's left leads. 2. **Dummy**: Declarer's partner lays cards face up. Declarer plays both hands. 3. **Trick Rules**: Must follow suit if possible. Highest trump or led suit wins. 4. **Scoring**: If contract is made, ALL tricks over 6 score towards the game (e.g., if you bid 1 and win 3, all 3 count toward the game).
keyRules: Trick Values: No Trump (10), Spades (9), Hearts (8), Diamonds (7), Clubs (6).
Honors: High cards (A, K, Q, J, 10 of trumps) score separate bonus points 'Above the Line'.
Rubber: The first team to win two games of 30 points each wins the Rubber bonus (250 points).

strategy.basic: Bidding is less about hand-strength accuracy than in Contract Bridge. The goal is primarily to reach the 30-point threshold for a game as cheaply as possible.
strategy.intermediate: Overtrick Strategy: Since overtricks count toward the game, you can bid conservatively. A bid of '1 No Trump' potentially scores the whole game (30 pts) if you take 9 tricks.
strategy.advanced: Defensive Doubling: Double an opponent if you are certain they cannot make their bid, but be waryâ€”if they make it, the doubled tricks may win them the game immediately.
tips: In No Trump hands, prioritize long suits to set up 'low' trick-winners after high cards are gone.
Don't ignore the honors. In Auction, the honor bonus (e.g., 4 honors in one hand = 80-100 pts) is often larger than the trick score.

variations.name: Nullos
variations.description: A variation where a player bids to lose tricks. Ranking usually falls between Spades and No Trump.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variation describes null-style contracts; base engine already models bidding and trick play so no overrides yet.

scoring.description: Score is divided into 'Above the Line' (bonuses/honors) and 'Below the Line' (tricks toward game).
scoring.winCondition: The partnership with the highest cumulative total (Above + Below) after a team wins two games wins the Rubber.

synthesis.shortDescription: Step back into the golden age of card games with Auction Bridge. Master the competitive auction, manage your honors, and claim the 250-point Rubber bonus in this refined precursor to modern Bridge.

hero.title: AUCTION BRIDGE
hero.subtitle: The Edwardian Classic
